script: The most famous painting on earth was a nobody until a handyman stole it. In 1911, the Mona Lisa hung in the Louvre, mostly ignored. Tourists walked right past it. Then a museum handyman named Vincenzo Peruggia hid in a closet overnight. In the morning he tucked it under his coat and walked out the front door. Nobody noticed it was gone for a full day. When they did, police questioned Pablo Picasso and let him go. Here's the part nobody mentions. The empty wall became the attraction. Crowds lined up to stare at the blank space where it used to hang. Newspapers printed that face on every front page for two years. Peruggia kept it in a trunk in his apartment, six blocks from the museum, for twenty-eight months. He was caught trying to sell it to a dealer in Florence. He got seven months in jail. The Louvre got the most valuable accident in history. Ever since, it has hung behind bulletproof glass, watched by guards day and night, while the crowd photographs a painting nobody wanted. All because a handyman turned a nobody into the most famous painting on earth.

title: The Mona Lisa Was a Nobody Until a Janitor Stole It
description:
In 1911 the Mona Lisa was just another painting in the Louvre. Then a handyman walked out with it under his coat, and the empty wall drew bigger crowds than the painting ever had.

What made it priceless: the art, or the theft?
